slides.photo_brief: Best WIDE mountain photo with Isha IN it. Kinnaur Kailash range behind her, morning light. This is the thumbnail of the whole post.
slides.kicker: 3 Himachal villages that feel like another planet
slides.title: KALPA

slides.photo_brief: The Kinnaur Kailash peaks at sunrise (golden glow), OR Isha looking out at them. Vertical if possible.
slides.line: I woke up to the whole Kinnaur Kailash range turning gold — straight from the window, no filter, no crowd.
slides.note: that tall one is Kinner Kailash, ~6,050 m

slides.photo_brief: Old Kalpa character shot — apple orchard, old wooden houses, the monastery/temple, or the road to Roghi village.
slides.note: Stay up in old Kalpa, not down in Reckong Peo. Walk to Roghi village for the view they call 'Suicide Point' — the drop is unreal. Mornings in Apr–Jun give the clearest peaks.
slides.confirm: Where exactly did you stay in Kalpa? Swap the stay line for the real name/area if you want to name it.

slides.photo_brief: Wide Baspa valley shot with the wooden houses of Chitkul, Isha in frame if you have one.
slides.title: CHITKUL
slides.line: the last inhabited village before the Indo–Tibet border

slides.photo_brief: The Baspa river, or Isha by the river / in the potato fields. Cold, clean, blue-grey light.
slides.line: The Baspa running ice-cold, the cleanest air I’ve ever breathed, and a silence that makes you forget your phone exists.
slides.note: 3,450 m · end of the old trade route

slides.photo_brief: The 'Last Dhaba of Hindustan' board, the Mathi Devi wooden temple, or a plate of food by the river.
slides.note: Eat at the 'Hindustan ka Aakhri Dhaba', sit by the Baspa with chai, and come May–October — the road shuts with the first snow.
slides.confirm: Did you actually eat at the last dhaba? If not, I'll soften this to a general 'don't skip' line.

slides.photo_brief: Tosh village on the slope with the snow peaks at the head of Parvati valley. Wide.
slides.title: TOSH
slides.line: where Parvati valley simply runs out of road

slides.photo_brief: Cafe / balcony view over the valley, chai or maggi in hand, snow peaks in the distance.
slides.line: Slow mornings, chai with a snow-peak view, and nowhere you have to be. Tosh is the full stop at the end of the valley.
slides.note: park at Barshaini, walk up the last bit

slides.photo_brief: A strong closing wide — Isha with the valley behind her, or the peaks at golden hour.
slides.note: Stay a night higher up for sunrise on the peaks, and walk to Kutla for an even quieter view.
